sections.title: The Search for Wisdom
observations: Job reflects on the value of wisdom and how it is sought after by humanity.
He describes the lengths to which people go to find precious metals and resources, emphasizing that wisdom is far more valuable than material wealth.
Job illustrates that while humans can mine the earth for gold and silver, they cannot find wisdom in the same way.

sections.title: The Inaccessibility of Wisdom
observations: Job continues to elaborate on the elusive nature of wisdom, stating that it cannot be found in the land of the living or among the creatures of the earth.
He points out that even the depths of the sea and the heights of the mountains do not contain wisdom, highlighting its transcendence.
This section emphasizes that wisdom is not a commodity that can be bought or sold; it is beyond human reach.

sections.title: The Divine Source of Wisdom
observations: In this section, Job reveals that true wisdom is found only in God.
He states that God understands the way to wisdom and knows its place, indicating that wisdom is part of God's divine order.
Job concludes that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, underscoring the relationship between reverence for God and the acquisition of true understanding.

importantVerses.commentary: But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
And he said to man, 'Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.'

questions: What does Job's description of the search for wisdom reveal about human nature and our priorities?
How does the inaccessibility of wisdom challenge our understanding of knowledge and understanding in our lives?
In what ways can we cultivate a fear of the Lord as the foundation for wisdom in our daily lives?
